$comment: Machine-readable surface contract for all w6w wrappers. Source of truth for conformance tests. Keep in sync with docs/endpoints.md.
$basePathComment: Empty since 0.2.0: the server serves its routes at the ROOT of its own host (https://api.w6w.io/vars, not .../api/vars). Clients append nothing to the configured origin.

operations.name: me
operations.summary: Caller identity plus w6w component versions.
operations.notes: Fixed 2026-07-28: the wrapper calls `/auth/me` directly — the server’s real, already-live identity route (verified live: 200, `{tenant, subject, account, role}`), not the not-yet-built `/api/me` alias D15 originally specced. `{tenant, subject, account, role}`. The response body is flat, NOT a `{user:{…}}` envelope. The live consumer is the reference studio; a nested envelope would break it. `versions` is optional and additive — the server does not send one today, so a wrapper must tolerate it being absent entirely and must tolerate unknown keys inside it when it does. `versions.wrapper` is filled client-side from the wrapper’s own package version. PRECEDENCE IS SERVER-WINS: the wrapper’s own version is only a DEFAULT that any key the server supplied overrides — `{ wrapper: VERSION, ...body.versions }` in TS, `{"wrapper": VERSION, **(body.get("versions") or {})}` in Python. Do NOT write the other order (`{**server, wrapper: VERSION}`), which would make the wrapper’s value win; the two are observably different on the one field a bug report is read off. DISPLAY IS A SEPARATE RULE: a wrapper must never SHOW a version of `0.0.0` or empty — if the resolved value is `0.0.0` or empty string, it presents `"dev"` (D5). The two rules do not conflict, because they act at different layers: server-wins governs the VALUE carried in the returned object (which stays a faithful transcription of the wire), the display rule governs what a banner such as `w6w info` PRINTS. So a server sending `versions.wrapper: "0.0.0"` is carried through in the data and rendered as `dev` to the user. D8 — the operation name is `me`; `w6w info` is a CLI alias only (see `cliAlias`).

operations.name: connections.list
operations.notes: `credential` and `lastRefreshedAt` are redacted server-side and must not appear in the wrapper's list type. D4 — kept in v0.1.0 even though the 07-27 intake does not name it: without it a user has no way to discover a `conn_…` URN to pass to `run`. Verified live.

operations.name: workflows.list
operations.notes: Unpaginated today. Return a container type that can grow a cursor without a breaking change. D4 — kept in v0.1.0: it is how a user discovers a `wf_…` URN to pass to `run`. Verified live.

operations.name: workflows.run
operations.summary: Enqueue a workflow run; optionally wait for a terminal state.

params.name: trigger
params.$comment: `knownValues` is DOCUMENTATION, not a constraint. `closedEnum: false` — wrappers type this as a plain string and must NOT validate against the list; the server may add a sixth value and a wrapper that hard-codes the enum would reject a request the server accepts.

operations.notes: 202 is a normal outcome, not an error: the run is still queued/running. A failed run returns 200 with status 'failed' and must NOT raise. `trigger` is a STRING, not an object: the server reads it as a `RunTrigger` (`"manual" | "schedule" | "webhook" | "event" | "replay"` today), and it defaults to 'manual' server-side when omitted. The five values are recorded in `knownValues` as documentation only — every wrapper types the param as an open string (`trigger?: string` / `trigger: str | None`) and passes it through unvalidated, so a sixth server value needs no wrapper release. `variables` and `input` are NOT interchangeable: `variables` seeds the run's variable scope, read downstream as `vars.*`; `input` is delivered to the entry trigger node's own recorded output, read downstream as `steps.<triggerId>.output.<key>` — the shape a trigger's declared fields actually arrive in. D4 — kept alongside the unified `run`, which is deliberately narrower: `?wait=`, `variables`, `trigger` and `input` have no slot in the three-field `{urn, action, payload}` shape. Verified live.

operations.name: documents.list
operations.summary: List the caller's documents in a project.
operations.notes: Server wraps the body as `{ documents: Doc[] }`; the wrapper unwraps and returns the array. Documents ARE project-scoped: every `documents.*` route accepts an optional `?project=` and otherwise resolves the account's default project. An unknown project id is `400 unknown_project`.

operations.name: documents.get
operations.summary: Fetch one document by its `doc_…` id.
operations.notes: Addressed by the server-issued `doc_…` id, not by `key` (D6 — wrappers mirror the server's addressing exactly). Server wraps the body as `{ document: Doc }`; the wrapper unwraps. Missing id is `404 unknown_document`.

operations.name: documents.getByKey
operations.summary: Fetch one document by its human-chosen `key`.
operations.notes: `DocumentsRepo.getByKey` already existed and was already called by `POST /documents` for its conflict check; only the HTTP route was missing. D12 (amending D6) — a user who chose a key should be able to address by it, and the alternative leaks internal `doc_…` ids to users who never saw them. NO client-side list-then-filter: `packages/wrappers/README.md` "What a wrapper is" forbids composing two calls to make an operation useful. Same wrap/unwrap and `404 unknown_document` as `documents.get`. Server-implemented 2026-07-28: the route trims the incoming key to match what `POST /documents` stores, and creation rejects a key of exactly "." or ".." — the one class no HTTP client can round-trip through a URL path segment (percent-encoding is a no-op on `.`, and different clients disagree on dot-segment collapse).

operations.name: documents.create
operations.summary: Create a document under a caller-chosen `key`.
operations.notes: Create is addressed by `key` (D6 — mirror the server: create by key, update/delete by id). `key` is a non-empty string of at most 128 characters, unique per scope+project. `content` is raw text and is never parsed. `format` is one of text|markdown|yaml|html|json and defaults to 'text'; it is a hint only and does not gate the content. Duplicate key is `409 document_exists` — wrappers must surface that code, not swallow it into a generic error.

operations.name: documents.update
operations.summary: Patch a document's content, format or description.
operations.notes: Addressed by the `doc_…` id, NOT by `key` (D6). `key` itself is immutable — it is not in the patch body. Every field is optional; an omitted field is left alone. Missing id is `404 unknown_document`.

operations.name: documents.delete
operations.notes: Addressed by the `doc_…` id (D6). The server returns `{ ok: true }`, but the wrapper unwraps it to NOTHING: the declared return is `void` (`Promise<void>` in TS, `None` in Python, no stdout payload in the CLI beyond an exit code). `Ok` is not a public wrapper type — see docs/implementation.md §5. Deleting an unknown id is `404 unknown_document`, not a silent success — the delete is not idempotent and wrappers must not pretend otherwise.

operations.name: vars.list
operations.notes: Vars are NOT project-scoped — unlike documents, no `vars.*` route accepts `?project=` (verified: no `vars` route reads it). They are scoped by tenant/subject only. Do not add a `project` option to any `vars.*` signature; adding one later would be additive, faking one now would be a lie the server does not honour. Server wraps the body as `{ vars: Var[] }`; the wrapper unwraps.

operations.name: vars.get
operations.summary: Fetch one variable by its `var_…` id.
operations.notes: Addressed by the server-issued `var_…` id, not by `name` (D6). Server wraps the body as `{ var: Var }`; the wrapper unwraps — note the singular key is `var`, which is a reserved word in TypeScript and must be read as a property, never destructured into a binding of that name. Missing id is `404 unknown_var`.

operations.name: vars.getByName
operations.summary: Fetch one variable by its human-chosen `name`.
operations.notes: `VarsRepo.getByName` already existed and was already called by `POST /vars` for its conflict check; only the HTTP route was missing. D12 (amending D6) — key-addressed reads become server routes rather than client-side composition; `packages/wrappers/README.md` "What a wrapper is" forbids a list-then-filter workaround. Same `404 unknown_var` as `vars.get`. Server-implemented 2026-07-28: names are already regex-validated (`[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*`) at create time, which is URL-safe by construction — no extra hazard handling needed.

operations.name: vars.create
operations.summary: Create a typed variable under a caller-chosen `name`.
operations.notes: Create is addressed by `name` (D6 — mirror the server: create by name, update/delete by id). `name` must match `^[a-z_][a-z0-9_]*$`; violations are `400 invalid_name`. `type` is one of string|number|boolean|json and `value` is validated against it server-side (`400 invalid_type` / `400 invalid_value`). Duplicate name is `409 var_exists` — wrappers must surface that code, not swallow it into a generic error. No `project` param: vars are not project-scoped.

operations.name: vars.update
operations.summary: Patch a variable's type, value or description.
operations.notes: Addressed by the `var_…` id, NOT by `name` (D6). `name` itself is immutable — it is not in the patch body. A `value` sent without a `type` is validated against the variable's EXISTING type. Missing id is `404 unknown_var`. No `project` param: vars are not project-scoped.

operations.name: vars.delete
operations.notes: Addressed by the `var_…` id (D6). The server returns `{ ok: true }`, but the wrapper unwraps it to NOTHING: the declared return is `void` (`Promise<void>` in TS, `None` in Python, no stdout payload in the CLI beyond an exit code). `Ok` is not a public wrapper type — see docs/implementation.md §5. Deleting an unknown id is `404 unknown_var`, not a silent success. No `project` param: vars are not project-scoped.

operations.name: functions.run
operations.summary: Run one Function by its key (or id) and return its output.
operations.notes: The NAME IS THE FIRST ARGUMENT in every lane, matching `workflows.run(id, opts?)`, so all three runnable kinds read alike; it is not a field inside an options object. Wrappers expose the body field as `payload` even though the wire spells it `inputs` — one word across every runnable kind, and reconciling that inconsistency is precisely the wrapper's job (the Endpoint operation below spells the same concept `input`). Returns the Function's OUTPUT, not a kind-discriminated envelope: the kind is settled by the operation name, so a discriminant would be a field the caller unwraps to learn nothing. A `null` output is a SUCCESSFUL run, not a malformed body — a Function's output is an opaque pass-through and an action that returns nothing yields `{"output": null}` — so a wrapper must guard on PRESENCE of the `output` key rather than on its truthiness. 422 `function_incomplete` when the Function has no runnable `impl`. The `{idOrKey}` path segment takes EITHER the resource's host-issued id or the key the user gave it, with no prefix, flag or tag to say which — the two shapes cannot collide, because an id carries a kind prefix and therefore an underscore while a key is a kebab-slug that forbids one. Resolution is id-first (a pure prefix test, no query), so this path cannot be used to probe whether a key exists by supplying something id-shaped. Two unknown KEYS answer identically and neither is echoed back — a key is short, human-chosen and guessable, so echoing it would make this an enumeration oracle; an unknown id may still be echoed, since nobody guesses a uuid. The key is unique per ACCOUNT, so within the scope a credential carries it names exactly one resource.

operations.name: endpoints.run
operations.summary: Run one Endpoint by its key (or id); the envelope's kind says which arm answered.
operations.notes: Name-first, exactly like `functions.run`; wrappers expose the body field as `payload` though the wire spells it `input` (singular here, plural for a Function). UNLIKE `functions.run` this returns the kind-discriminated `RunEnvelope`, and the asymmetry is deliberate: an Endpoint dispatches to an app action, a Function or a Workflow, so only the response says which answered — the discriminant is information, not ceremony. The workflow arm returns 202, which is a NORMAL outcome and not an error. Wrappers must tolerate an unknown future `kind` rather than crashing, the same rule the unified `run` carries. The `{idOrKey}` path segment takes EITHER the resource's host-issued id or the key the user gave it, with no prefix, flag or tag to say which — the two shapes cannot collide, because an id carries a kind prefix and therefore an underscore while a key is a kebab-slug that forbids one. Resolution is id-first (a pure prefix test, no query), so this path cannot be used to probe whether a key exists by supplying something id-shaped. Two unknown KEYS answer identically and neither is echoed back — a key is short, human-chosen and guessable, so echoing it would make this an enumeration oracle; an unknown id may still be echoed, since nobody guesses a uuid. The key is unique per ACCOUNT, so within the scope a credential carries it names exactly one resource.

operations.name: run
operations.summary: Run anything addressable by URN — a connection action, a function, an endpoint or a workflow.
operations.notes: D3 — `RunEnvelope` is kind-discriminated with exactly three arms: `{kind:"action", value}` | `{kind:"function", output}` | `{kind:"workflow", runId, status}`. The action and function arms return 200; the workflow arm returns 202, and 202 is a NORMAL outcome, not an error — the run is queued, and `runId` is how the caller follows it. Wrappers must switch on `kind` and must tolerate an unknown future `kind` rather than crashing. `action` is optional because a workflow, function or endpoint URN has no action; it is required in practice for a `conn_…` URN. `urn` resolves over the `conn_`, `wf_`, `fn_` and `ep_` arms (D16), and, additionally, an account-scoped alias name (kebab-slug, `_`-free, which is why no flag is needed to disambiguate the two); `doc_` and `var_` are NOT URN arms in v0.1.0 and are addressed by the `documents.*` / `vars.*` operations above. This is deliberately narrower than `workflows.run`: `?wait=`, `variables` and `trigger` have no slot in the three-field `{urn, action, payload}` shape (D4). Server-implemented 2026-07-28: a third sibling BLL service dispatching to the same runners the dedicated invoke routes use — no new execution path, no change to core Callable.

cli.$comment: CLI-only surface. Not API operations — requirements the CLI wrapper must satisfy. See docs/cli.md.

help.notes: --help must resolve with no token set and no server reachable. Unknown or incomplete commands print the relevant help to stderr and exit 1.

exitCodes.0: success, including help and a queued/running workflow

outOfScope: all write operations on connections and workflows
